# LLM overall accuracy — Claude triage on the 147-gene bench

> **Supplementary Figure 2.** Supplying protein-coding gene identifiers, but not web search or pre-fetched PubMed abstracts, drives within-tier accuracy gains in language-model triage on the 147-protein benchmark. Bars show mean soft-credit verdict accuracy across replicates. Eight Claude models (Haiku 4.5 and 5.5; Sonnet 4.6, 5 and 5.5; Opus 4.8, 5 and 5.5) are compared under up to four conditions: gene symbol alone (naive); symbol plus a cached gene summary and stable HGNC/UniProt identifiers (+IDs); identifier context plus an on-demand web-search tool; and identifier context plus PubMed abstract excerpts retrieved in advance and appended to the prompt. Opus 5.5 was also run with identifiers at low reasoning effort. Three replicates per protein per condition (points; error bars SEM). Refused calls (Opus 5.5 only) are excluded from accuracy, and the share refused is printed on the bar. Color indicates model generation, and lavender marks the two configurations the production pipeline uses. Sonnet 4.6 with identifiers is the production triage configuration.
<!-- END manuscript-legend -->

Bars showing overall verdict accuracy for each (model, prompt-variant)
Claude triage cell on the 147-gene bench. Grouped by model
(Haiku 4.5 / Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 4.6 / Sonnet 5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 4.8 /
Opus 5 / Opus 5.5); within each group, hatch encodes the prompt variant:

* solid — naive (gene symbol only)
* `//` — + IDs (cached gene summary + HGNC/UniProt identifiers)
* `xx` — + IDs + web (identifier context plus a web-search tool)
* `..` — + IDs + PubMed (identifier context plus PubMed retrieval)
* `\\` — + IDs, low effort (the + IDs prompt at low reasoning effort)

Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 4.6 were run on all four context variants; Haiku
5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 4.8 on naive and + IDs; Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 on
+ IDs only; and Opus 5.5 on + IDs at its default and at low reasoning
effort. Groups are packed, so a model with fewer variants takes less
width.

Color encodes model generation (orange Claude 4.x, blue Claude 5, teal
Claude 5.5; darker = larger model). The two configurations the
production pipeline uses, Sonnet 4.6 + IDs and + IDs + PubMed, are
lavender.

Refused calls — a safety classifier declining to answer, which only Opus
5.5 does on this bench — are excluded from accuracy, and the share of
calls refused is printed on the bar.

Each cell was run three times per gene. Bar height is the mean of the
three per-replicate accuracies; the points are the individual
replicates and the error bars are the SEM across replicates.

Accuracy uses the project's soft-credit rule: yes ≡ contextual on
the positive side; `no` matches `no` only.

Run:

```
uv run make_db_correctness_overall.py
```

Data: the bundled `db_correctness_overall.tsv` next to the script (no
download). One row per gene × model × prompt variant × replicate, with
the soft-credit `is_match` and the ground-truth verdict and class
joined in. The canonical copy is
`data/processed/figures/db_correctness_overall.tsv`, built by
`scripts/build_figure_tsvs.py`.

Canonical in-repo generator:
[`scripts/figures/db_correctness_overall.py`](https://github.com/Deliverome-Project/accessible-surfaceome/blob/main/scripts/figures/db_correctness_overall.py).
